newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- NOV 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- NOV 15.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--The budget and other economic measures will be announced gradually over the next two weeks so as to diffuse any possible adverse political reaction, particularly from within ruling party PASOK. The first official statements by Prime Minister Costas Simitis and National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou will follow the cabinet meeting to be held on Tuesday.
--Despite progress, the Greek economy continues to need particularly harsh and continuing efforts to meet convergence criteria, the European Monetary Institute says in its report, released last week.

--The government is planning on more strictly regulating who trades on the Athens Stock Exchange by requiring brokerage firms to deposit guarantees in the form of cash, state titles or letters of credit.

--The government is now facing a 350 billion drachma suit filed by the Athens Casino consortium for breach of contract, after the development ministry revoked the licence for the casino at Floisvos earlier this year.
IMERISIA

--The last auction of non-taxable state titles will be held on November 22, with interest rates down by a further 0.30 percent. The base rate will fall to 12.0 percent from 12.30 percent. Taxation on interest from titles will begin in December, sources say.

--The government is to abolish provisions that lead to the imprisonment of persons for personal debts. Detention of debtors to the state, however, will remain, and the finance ministry is moving to pursue debtors to the Greek state residing abroad.
--A new solution to the prickly issue of extended trading hours appears to favour stores open till 5.30 p.m. on Saturday.
KERDOS

--The Athens bourse dips 3.3 percent and there are fears of a continuation today. The disappointing results of the first full day of trading at the bourse following its closure last week are being attributed to the climate of distrust prevailing amongst investors and to the loss of credibility in the institution itself.

--The government has decided not to index income scales or to impose 'indirect' taxes for the time being. The question, however, of a special charge has been held over until the Cabinet discussion on Tuesday.
--The National Bank of Greece predicts a 45 billion drachma profit in 1996.
EXPRESS

--The crisis sinks the bourse: the bourse's general price index falls 34 points. At the same time, the ASE administration announced that negotiations on the shares of the four firms appeared to be involved in the 'Delta affair' will be postponed for the moment.
--Income scales for self-employed professionals will be cost-of-living indexed, according to sources. The finance ministry will announce the decision shortly.
--How much to cut the interest rates and spreads of the 200 billion drachma bond auction set for next week is what is worrying the finance ministry at the moment.
NAFTEMBORIKI

--Representatives of Delta Securities are to appear to plead before a prosecutor in the following few days while, reports say, the joint-surety fund is also expected to file suit against Delta and other implicated firms. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
